title: Citropten from Citrus sinensis peel protects against obstructive chronic kidney disease: insights from network pharmacology and experimental validation.
authors: Talati, Yugant Krishnakumar; Gaikwad, Anil Bhanudas
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用网络药理学和实验验证探讨柑橘提取物Citropten对慢性肾病的保护作用，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a global health challenge affecting millions, yet effective therapeutic options remain scarce. This study explores the renoprotective potential of citropten (CTP), a citrus-derived coumarin derivative isolated from the peel of Citrus sinensis, using an integrated in silico and in vivo strategy. Pharmacokinetic screening indicated that CTP possesses favourable drug-likeness, oral bioavailability, and a safety profile. Network pharmacology identified 188 CTP-associated CKD targets, generating a robust interaction network with an average node degree of 12, from which 13 hub targets were identified. Pathway enrichment analyses showed that these targets are predominantly involved in inflammatory, mitophagy, and fibrotic signalling pathways. Transcriptomic validation showed that 9 of 13 hub targets were dysregulated in CKD, reinforcing their clinical relevance. Molecular docking suggested strong interactions between CTP and key regulatory proteins, particularly MAPK14, NFE2L2, and PARP1. These computational findings were experimentally validated in a unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) rat model of CKD. Oral administration of CTP (10 and 20 mg kg(-1) day(-1) for 21 days) significantly preserved kidney function and histological architecture. CTP treatment also significantly attenuated extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), indicating reduced renal fibrosis. Mechanistic evaluation of hub targets demonstrated that CTP effectively modulated the Nrf2/NF-kappaB1/PARP1 signalling axis, a pivotal regulator of oxidative stress and inflammation. Consistent with pathway prediction, downstream validation revealed that CTP activated PINK1/Parkin/LC3B-mediated mitophagy, thereby restoring mitochondrial quality. Collectively, these findings suggest that CTP is a promising food-derived, multi-target bioactive candidate with potential therapeutic relevance for CKD management.
abstract_zh: 慢性肾脏病（CKD）是一项影响数百万人的全球健康挑战，然而有效的治疗选择仍然稀缺。本研究采用整合的计算机模拟与体内策略，探讨了从柑橘（Citrus sinensis）果皮中分离的柑橘香豆素衍生物——柠檬油素（CTP）的肾脏保护潜力。药代动力学筛选表明，CTP具有良好的类药性、口服生物利用度和安全性特征。网络药理学鉴定了188个CTP相关的CKD靶点，生成了一个平均节点度为12的稳健相互作用网络，从中识别出13个枢纽靶点。通路富集分析显示，这些靶点主要参与炎症、线粒体自噬和纤维化信号通路。转录组验证表明，13个枢纽靶点中有9个在CKD中表达失调，进一步强化了其临床相关性。分子对接提示CTP与关键调控蛋白之间存在强相互作用，尤其是MAPK14、NFE2L2和PARP1。这些计算发现在单侧输尿管梗阻（UUO）大鼠CKD模型中得到了实验验证。口服CTP（10和20 mg kg(-1) day(-1)，持续21天）显著保护了肾功能和组织学结构。CTP治疗还显著减轻了细胞外基质（ECM）积累和上皮-间质转化（EMT），表明肾纤维化减少。对枢纽靶点的机制评估表明，CTP有效调节了Nrf2/NF-kappaB1/PARP1信号轴，这是氧化应激和炎症的关键调控因子。与通路预测一致，下游验证揭示CTP激活了PINK1/Parkin/LC3B介导的线粒体自噬，从而恢复线粒体质量。综合来看，这些发现表明CTP是一种有前景的食物来源、多靶点生物活性候选物，对CKD管理具有潜在治疗意义。
